data.note: Fix retry-refusals count: dedup blocks 2nd identical claim.force; count refusals across filings
Unspent approvals owner-gated + 3600s TTL strands re-claims; allow successor lane spend / lengthen TTL

data.claim: pending_for dedups an unchanged re-file to the same pending ask, so refusals() counts one unresolved ask forever
data.falsifier: R.file(..., dedupe=False) returns a NEW ask id for an identical still-pending canon
data.mechanism: with the threshold armed, consume.operator_gate files a retry verb with dedupe=False so each re-file is a NEW ask and refusals() accumulates
data.probe_output: deduped same: True; no-dedupe new: True; refusals: 1; retry_armed(on): True
data.question: Why does auto_approve_after_retries never auto-approve a live agent retrying an unchanged claim.force?

evidence.note: claim CONFIRMED: dedup deduplicates an unchanged retry-verb re-file to the same pending ask; probe /tmp/repro1.py refutes('falsifier') by a NEW ask id under dedupe=False

data.claim: the approval digest binds the agent and the spend is owner-gated to the requester, so a successor lane re-running the same action is refused
data.mechanism: drop the actor from the canonical record (digest binds the action) and drop the requested_by gate so a successor spending the same verb+item+target+state is authorised by digest+judge
data.probe_output: agent in digest: True (same digest across agents); successor spent: True
data.question: Why is a granted claim.force/complete.force approval orphaned when its requesting lane dies?
